content.intro: Bitwise Operators is lesson 32 in Operators and Expressions. An operator combines values or expressions according to defined rules. Use parentheses when they make intent easier to see, especially when several operators interact.
content.why_it_matters: Operators are compact expressions of behavior. Understanding evaluation order prevents subtle bugs. This lesson focuses on bitwise operators and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates bitwise operators. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.

At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for bitwise operators before editing the code.

content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.
